tasks.short: Arrange rental services and accept returns

steps.what: Rent items, arrange services and inspect and accept physical returns
Record handover or returns and pass confirmed arrangements to the service team

tasks.design: Use native item scanning and handover or return forms in the {OTHER} rental system. Retain physical transfer, condition judgement and service agreement; the clerk captures the facts and checks the record before updating status.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual item selection and repeated handover fields add screen effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Rental systems support item histories and barcode check-in.
tasks.still_hard: Damage disputes, incomplete returns and uncertain readiness for the next rental.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk inspects the actual item and agrees next steps with the customer.
tasks.altitude: Less record navigation without changing physical or customer responsibilities.

evidence.claim: Booqable provides item rental history and barcode check-in; the proposed labour saving is not measured by that capability description.

assumptions: Boundary is handover or return and related status capture, not reservation, payment or aggregate transaction reporting. Record these events once in a roll-up.

Clerk s1 produces actual item identity, observed condition, missing accessories and agreed arrangements through inspection. s2 captures order ID, item ID, event type, timestamp, condition, holds and instruction recipient; capture and approval retain 21 hours.
A barcode identifies an item, not its condition. Clerk enters condition explicitly; missing codes or uncertain facts require manual lookup, not a free ready-to-rent flag.
Test native scans and forms before custom code. No automatic damage charge or release of unsafe equipment is introduced.
research_questions: Does scanning reduce record effort while preserving physical condition checks?

already_counted.description: Capture condition, resolve scan exceptions and approve records

approvals.approved_version: Exact order, item, event, condition, hold and service instruction checked before status update; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=70+21=91. Gross 9 minus 1 upkeep gives net 8. Low assumes native scanning already used; high requires repeated manual selection within the 30-hour record slice. Physical handover and inspection retain 70 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Count customers entering and capture the establishment's visitor totals
Keep transaction records and combine them with customer counts
Check daily transaction records and customer totals for gaps or duplicates

tasks.design: Keep the existing visitor tally and use a native export from the {OTHER} till or rental system. A deterministic import updates the {SPREADSHEET} activity record with duplicate checks; the clerk enters counts and resolves discrepancies.
tasks.previous_blocker: A separate daily record can require transaction rekeying even though the source system already holds transactions.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured exports can remove this duplicate transcription.
tasks.still_hard: Visitor counts are not the same as transaction counts, and incomplete source records need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk recognises counting gaps and unusual corrections.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate transcription; counting and record accountability remain.

reach.task: Trace a missing transaction to a register receipt

evidence.claim: A deterministic source-to-record import can remove duplicate transcription; the assumed manual daily record and saving require local verification.

assumptions: Boundary is visitor counting and a separate activity record, not original sale, reservation or return capture. Existing system runtime earns no saving.

Counter staff produce original transaction ID, date, type, amount and status during ordinary transaction processing, whose capture remains unchanged in its own task. s2 clerk checks the export schema and captures store/date/interval/count from s1 within 12 retained hours.
Clerk s1 produces visitor counts by the existing method; all 40 hours remain. No door sensor, camera or structured footfall feed is assumed.
Try native combined reports before custom import. If no duplicate record exists, use the low scenario. Missing exports or schema mismatches require manual recording rather than fabricated totals.
unknowns: Whether a separate duplicate activity record exists
research_questions: Can a native report replace rekeying while keeping visitor and transaction counts distinct?

already_counted.description: Capture count fields and handle import exceptions
Check totals and investigate missing or duplicate events

incremental.description: Maintain import mapping and reconciliation checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=40+12+20=72. Gross 28 less 2 upkeep gives net 26. High requires 40 hours of duplicate record work reducible to 12; low assumes native records already suffice. Original transactions and visitor counting earn no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Reserve items and maintain rental records

steps.what: Confirm requested rental items, times and customer details
Check availability and reserve items for the requested times
Keep records of items rented against the committed reservation

tasks.design: Use the {OTHER} rental system as the reservation and rental-history record. Configure availability-aware booking and reuse its committed record instead of maintaining a second document; the clerk captures the request and checks the booking before commitment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability checking and a separate register can repeat the same reservation facts.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing rental systems combine item availability with rental history.
tasks.still_hard: Simultaneous reservations, maintenance holds and changed return times.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk confirms what the customer means and resolves unavailable-item choices.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate reservation paperwork without new booking authority.

reach.task: Confirm the correct accessory set for a reserved item

evidence.claim: Booqable tracks item availability and rental history; it supports the proposed single rental record.

assumptions: Boundary is reservation and its register, not physical handover, condition capture or reporting. If generic order intake already includes this exact booking, allocate its hours once in the roll-up.
Clerk produces checked item, customer, quantity and start/end times in s1; s2 captures these fields and checks maintenance holds and current availability within 31.5 retained hours.

Existing counter staff produce prior reservations and return statuses; equipment staff produce maintenance holds through unchanged operational capture. If status is stale, clerk verifies manually; no ready-to-rent flag is inferred.
s3 uses the exact committed reservation from s2. Its retained 8 hours cover checking the native record and exceptions, not recapturing the request.
Test native booking and history before custom code; simultaneous requests must be resolved by the source system's booking controls.
unknowns: Whether a second register is maintained
research_questions: Can the native committed record replace the second register without losing rental history?

already_counted.description: Capture reservation fields, resolve conflicts and approve booking
Check rental history record and correct exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain booking rules and record checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact customer, item IDs, quantities, start/end times and booking conditions checked before reservation commitment; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=35+31.5+8=74.5. Gross 25.5 less 1.5 upkeep gives net 24. Low assumes native booking and history already used; high requires repeated booking navigation and a second register. Request clarification retains 35 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify customer needs and shortlist products or services using the catalogue
Look up product and service facts for the candidate options
Recommend suitable products and services and explain relevant limitations

tasks.design: Configure catalogue filters and approved fact sheets in the {OTHER} counter system and {DOCS}. The clerk selects filters, checks facts and makes the recommendation; deterministic filtering does not decide suitability.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant features can be scattered across catalogue pages.
tasks.enabler_now: Native filters and linked fact sheets can reduce repeated factual lookup.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing price, practical fit and the customer's unstated constraints.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk probes needs and explains why an option may not fit.
tasks.altitude: Less catalogue search, with unchanged recommendation responsibility.

reach.task: Check an accessory suggestion against an approved compatibility table

evidence.claim: Deterministic catalogue filtering can assist factual lookup while leaving suitability judgement with the clerk. No measured saving is established here.

assumptions: Boundary is advice, not generic item-information delivery or order entry; allocate overlapping advice hours once in a roll-up.

Clerk produces categories and constraints in s1 and enters category, intended use, required dimensions or capacity and budget filters in s2. Capture and source checking remain within retained 9 hours.

Catalogue owner produces approved item/service ID, features, limits, price and version through unchanged catalogue maintenance; clerk upkeep covers new links. Missing facts lead to manual checking or specialist referral.
Test native filters before any custom code or model. The filter only retrieves matching facts and does not infer compatibility or customer suitability.
unknowns: Share of factual lookup in advice
research_questions: Does native filtering reduce lookup effort without weakening needs clarification or limitation explanations?

already_counted.description: Enter filters, verify sources and resolve lookup gaps

incremental.description: Maintain catalogue links and filter checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=40+9+45=94. Gross 6 less 1 upkeep gives net 5. Low assumes easy existing lookup or mostly conversational advice; high requires a 15-hour fact-search slice. Needs clarification and recommendations retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce duplicate rental records and factual searching while retaining physical handling and customer judgement.
reach: Trace transaction exceptions with a cashier
Check accessory identifiers with a parts salesperson
skills_to_grow: Check reservation and return data quality
Distinguish catalogue facts from suitability decisions
role.ambitious_version: Use one checked rental record from reservation through return while keeping customer commitments and equipment condition decisions personal.
